newsitem.title: COMOROS: Calm marks poll on Comoros constitution.
newsitem.headline: Calm marks poll on Comoros constitution.

text.p: People in the Comoros islands turned out in force on Sunday for the Indian Ocean island republic's latest poll on its constitution.
President Mohamed Taki, elected last March, wants voters to endorse his proposals for increasing the president's powers ahead of elections for a new national assembly.
Voters were asked: "Do you approve the constitution proposed by the president of the Republic?" Ballot papers were written in French and Arabic, the two official languages.
Five hours after polling began, some polling stations reported that over 95 per cent of eligible voters had cast their ballots, and no incidents were reported.
The referendum on the constitution is the fourth since independence in 1975 from France. There have been up to 17 coups or attempted coups.
Results of the referendum are expected to be announced on Monday.
Taki has ordered tough action against law-breakers, including the death penalty for murder, and has banned the sale of alcohol in the Islamic republic, except for diplomats and foreign tourists.
